keyFindings.text: A drift-proof inventory should join each command file to a normalized command id, owner, source metadata, aliases or retirement status and per-runtime enabled status, while keeping child route and runnable-target rows. Support: the current deriver combines metadata, compatibility inputs and doctor routes and validates bridge ids. Contrary evidence: multi-route doctor commands and MCP subroutes need target-level runnable data, so one flattened row per bridge would blur the command and route units. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/README.md:16-28] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/README.md:54-64] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:663-700]

The doctor family is the one fully connected slice: every derived doctor bridge is active in both scorers, and `doctor-phrase-reach.cjs` is the proof tool that each admitted phrase reaches its route. No equivalent reach proof exists for `/create:*`, `/deep:*`, `/design:*`, `/prompt:*` or `/speckit:*`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/README.md:64]

keyFindings.text: A drift-proof inventory needs one command-tree-derived registry with completeness as a hard gate: every command markdown must either carry owner metadata or have a written allow-list justification, and any bridge whose command spelling is absent from the tree must fail validation. The current deriver reads three independent inputs and never checks them against the live tree, so missing metadata, retired spellings and disabled entries remain invisible. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:21] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:87]

Ten command strings carry multiple bridge ids, all of them doctor routes, e.g. `/doctor:skill-advisor` → six ids (`…-tune`, `…-rebuild`, `…-skill-budget`, `…-skill-graph-freshness`, `…-router-reach`, `…-parent-skill`) [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:1]. So bridge ids are finer-grained than commands: one doctor command fronts 2-6 routable subcommands, while every other command is one id — a per-id recommendation surface cannot be turned into a per-command contract without a grouping key.

keyFindings.text: **Child sessions are ungated in the advisor path.** The spec gate implements `CHILD_SESSION_ENV = 'AI_SESSION_CHILD'` with `isChildSession(env)` and makes Gate 3 a no-op for a dispatched child [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/lib/spec-gate/spec-gate-core.mjs:101], but the advisor hook library contains no equivalent check — no `child`, `CHILD` or `lineage` guard exists in `hooks/lib` or the Claude adapter [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/lib/skill-advisor-cli-fallback.ts:190]. So a dispatched child (this lineage, for example) still receives advisor briefs, and a rule that says "run the command when the brief names one" would let a child start commands by itself — the exact failure the spec names.

Command-versus-skill ambiguity is by construction for non-doctor commands: `/speckit:plan a new feature for the login page` returns `command-spec-kit` at 0.82/0.20 and `system-spec-kit` at 0.82/0.18, which the ambiguity module treats as a tie because both gaps are within the 0.05 margins. The brief says "ambiguous" but carries no precedence rule for a command against its owner skill. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/ambiguity.ts:5] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/007-command-surfacing-and-workflow-enforcement/research/lineages/opencode-deepseek/iterations/iteration-003.md:17]

The prompt-policy replay fails on undertrigger when a positive gold row is declined, but does not assert that gold-none prompts abstain; the corpus scorer separately counts false fires on none. The replay is therefore not an overtrigger guard by itself. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/tests/prompt-policy-gold-replay.vitest.ts:44-83] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/score-routing-corpus.py:142-181]

Doctor bridges have a precedence rule that non-doctor bridges lack: a typed doctor command puts its own bridge first, a passing doctor bridge is placed after passing skills, and doctor bridges are removed before skill ambiguity and abstention are computed. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/fusion.ts:914] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/fusion.ts:1225]

**Over-triggering already has two guards.** `keepPassingSkillsAboveDoctorBridges()` demotes a doctor bridge below any passing skill unless one of its `lead_phrases` matches the prompt [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/fusion.ts:945], and the deriver rejects a `lead_phrases` entry that is not also in `trigger_phrases` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:328]. Both guards are doctor-only today, so generalising them is cheaper than inventing new ones.

Typed slash evidence holds the named command above a related dependency and suppresses false ambiguity, while the same words without slash syntax remain ambiguous. Keep ambiguity and action policy explicit: a high skill match alone does not resolve whether the command runs or asks under Gate 3. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/tests/scorer/typed-command-routing.vitest.ts:59-101] [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:60-68] [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:72-84]

A dispatched child session is the highest unsafe-run risk. `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` marks a non-interactive worker whose Gate 3 pre-resolves, and Law 4, Halt Conditions, Logic-Sync, Escalation and stop-for-yes become record-and-continue. A child that receives a "run command" brief can therefore start a mutating command with no user to answer the ask. [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:84]

**Bare-command recall is bounded by design.** `default_target` is allowed at most once per command, only on a multi-target command, and never on a mutating route, so a bare typed command never suggests a destructive target [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:52]. That is the existing precedent for "one safe entry point per command".

The deep-research command YAML owns the loop and dispatches a one-iteration leaf; the mode contract forbids nested CLI loops and the leaf definition denies Task/sub-agent dispatch. A child that re-enters the parent workflow can multiply work or recurse, so command routing should carry execution depth and leaf boundaries with the workflow. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/SKILL.md:82-90] [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/deep-research.md:61-67] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-auto.yaml:771-777]

**Ambiguity is first-class but skill-shaped.** The output carries `ambiguousWith`, `heldBelow` and a 120-token ambiguous brief form (iteration 3), and the baseline scores ambiguity top-1 at 20/24 with tau 0.03 [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/scorer-eval-baseline.json:1]; none of that machinery mentions commands, so a command/skill tie has to be expressed as a skill tie until the contract changes.

The lineage config sets maxIterations 10 and top-level stopPolicy max-iterations, but nested antiConvergence.stopPolicy says fail-closed; the workflow treats the iteration cap as the first terminal check. Keep one authoritative stop-policy value or test precedence, because conflicting stop fields can otherwise change whether convergence continues to the cap. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/007-command-surfacing-and-workflow-enforcement/research/lineages/codex-luna/deep-research-config.json:3-9] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/007-command-surfacing-and-workflow-enforcement/research/lineages/codex-luna/deep-research-config.json:96] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-auto.yaml:771-777]

The loop risk is real but only partly controlled. Gate 2's artifact trigger fires before every code or Markdown write, and command workflows write files, so a command workflow can re-enter routing on its own writes. Directive-lifecycle dedup suppresses a repeated brief to the same session, but it does not suppress repeated routing decisions. [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:68] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/skill-advisor-hook.md:40]

**A brief-to-command rule creates a real cycle.** `/doctor:skill-advisor tune` itself runs `advisor_recommend` and `advisor_validate` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:110]. If a brief can cause a command run, and a command can call the advisor, the graph is cyclic and nothing in the hooks counts depth or suppresses a re-entry.

The default brief cap is 80 tokens and the ambiguous branch requires a cap above 80; a command companion is omitted when it does not fit, while the directives and hygiene suffix are appended after the capped portion. Tests confirm both the companion-drop case and the fit case, so required command/action fields should not live only in an optional companion line. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:97-100] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:185-191] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:517-563] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/tests/doctor-brief-render.vitest.ts:57-64] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/tests/doctor-brief-render.vitest.ts:103-112]

The only anti-self-recommendation control is a -0.25 penalty against the advisor's own ids on audit or explainer prompts. It prevents the advisor from recommending itself, not a command workflow from routing back into the advisor. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/scoring-constants.ts:237]

Over-triggering is partly controlled: the no-slash penalty lowers every command candidate by 0.08 when the prompt has no slash, and the read-only gate keeps mutating commands at the explainer floor. The highest over-trigger surface is the doctor `lead_phrases` rule, which intentionally puts a passing bridge ahead of a passing skill; measured `disable comment hygiene gate` led with `/doctor:git hooks`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/fusion.ts:1197] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/README.md:48]

**The budget is headroom, not cap.** The routing head is capped at 80 tokens (120 ambiguous) and the 218-character directive rides outside the cap (iteration 3), so one added `→ /command (ask)` clause fits inside the existing 320-character head budget and does not require a cap change [INFERENCE: from the measured 50-character typical head and the 320-character cap].

**Dormant delivery turns a rule into a dead letter.** Cursor documents its dynamic adapter as dormant under the tested build and routes from a static rule (iteration 9), so any instruction conditioned on "when the brief names a command" silently does nothing on Cursor and Devin. The rule needs an explicit no-brief branch that asks the advisor directly.

The brief budget tolerates one command line and one policy marker; a third consequence line would compete with the fixed directive block and the ambiguity head inside the 120-token cap. The priority order should be command, then policy, then consequence only when space remains. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:97] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/007-command-surfacing-and-workflow-enforcement/research/lineages/opencode-deepseek/iterations/iteration-003.md:25]

**Dangling linkage is checked for ids and not for owners.** The bridge-resolution guard sweeps slash ids in aliases, phrase boosts and the Python scorer for dead commands [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/tests/command-bridge-resolution-guard.vitest.ts:1], yet nothing checks `ownerMode`: `sk-create-skill-parent` has no `SKILL.md` (iteration 7), `/memory:save` and `/spec_kit` have no command file (iteration 1), and 18 doctor bridges have no benchmark row (iteration 8). Three dead-reference classes, one guard.

Recommended controls: a same-owner precedence rule for command-versus-skill ties; a child authority scope in which a child may run only read-only or add-only commands and needs an explicit parent directive for mutating commands; a route-once guard per turn and command; a lead-phrase allowlist limited to diagnostic phrases; and a brief line order of command, policy, consequence. [INFERENCE: from findings 1-7]

Evidence against a blanket "command always wins" precedence: in the measured `/speckit:plan` case the skill has the lower uncertainty (0.18 against 0.20), so a command-first rule would override the better-calibrated candidate; the rule must be scoped to a command and its own owner skill, where the two are the same workflow wearing two names. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/007-command-surfacing-and-workflow-enforcement/research/lineages/opencode-deepseek/iterations/iteration-003.md:17]

The default confidence threshold is 0.8 with a 0.35 uncertainty ceiling. For "plan a new feature for the login page" the complete candidate set is `sk-doc` at 0.6202, `sk-code` at 0.5923, and `system-spec-kit` at 0.5887, so every candidate fails the 0.8 bar and `advisor_recommend` returns an empty list. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/compat/contract.ts:9] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/fusion.ts:1245]

The scorer subtracts 0.08 from command recommendations only in the sort comparator when the prompt contains no slash. Typed slash evidence has its own 0.55 explicit-lane floor, and graph support borrowed by a slash-anchored seed is capped below that seed. Tests confirm the concrete strings. This is useful, but it does not name route effects or whether to load, run, ask, or abstain. To surface all 45 commands, resolve the visible label from normalized command metadata and include its exact runnable form. The existing doctor map supports this pattern, but its fixed family scope contradicts using it unchanged for all commands. keyFindings.text: There is no `kind` and no runnable-command field anywhere in the public response; the only command-adjacent field is the optional `workflowMode`, which names a hub mode rather than a slash command [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/schemas/advisor-tool-schemas.ts:307]. The internal `AdvisorRecommendation.kind` seen in iteration 2 is dropped at this boundary because it is optional and not in the schema [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/subprocess.ts:41].

The brief has exactly two sentence forms and one fallback. Normal: `Advisor: {freshness}; use {label} {confidence}/{uncertainty} pass.`; ambiguous: `Advisor: {freshness}; ambiguous: {label} c/u vs {label} c/u pass.` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:567]. The operative verb is "use" in both, so the brief never instructs the model to run anything, and it never asks a question.

The hook contract says the brief is advisory and never replaces explicit skill loading; AGENTS Gate 2 separately says a confidence of at least 0.8 must invoke the skill and that explicit user direction can route it. The brief should distinguish “load this workflow now” from “ask which route/target” and from “recommend only.” Advisory-only behavior supports safe separation; the must-invoke rule contradicts leaving high-confidence command matches as passive suggestions. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/skill-advisor-hook.md:21] [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:63-70]

Measured briefs rendered `Also: /doctor:env list` for "check my environment variables" and `/doctor:git hooks` for "disable comment hygiene gate". This map is the only id-to-runnable translation in the renderer. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:109] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:219]

The brief therefore has no syntax that could express "the matching command is /speckit:plan" for the 28 non-doctor commands.

Measured: `/speckit:plan a new feature for the login page` produced `Advisor: live; ambiguous: command-spec-kit 0.82/0.20 vs system-spec-kit 0.82/0.18 pass.` The model sees a bridge id, not a runnable command. keyFindings.text: The renderer has a two-candidate ambiguous form and sanitizes instruction-shaped labels, while its token budget can omit a companion command. A contract should preserve the unresolved alternative or explicitly mark it truncated, expose typed confidence only, and avoid free-form reasons or raw prompts. Sanitization and the ambiguity form support this; the cap-dropping companion line is evidence against assuming every alternative survives. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:474-476] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:517-526] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:529-563]

The no-match or outage path adds a single /doctor:setup hint only for setup and health wording. The prior packet explicitly rejected placing a full route table in every fallback. Keep fallback prompt-specific and bounded, with a clean abstention when no route passes; the targeted setup hint supports a narrow fallback, while the static-list rejection contradicts generalizing it to all 45 commands. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/skill-advisor-hook.md:39-43] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/003-doctor-command-surfacing/001-doctor-command-guidance/research/research.md:178-179]

A renderer therefore cannot ask the payload whether a recommendation is a command or whether starting it is safe. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/schemas/advisor-tool-schemas.ts:295]

keyFindings.text: A model needs four facts to act on a command: a runnable invocation string (command plus mode and required arguments), a discriminator against the skill that also passed, a run-or-ask verdict, and a one-line consequence or undo note. The current brief supplies only the label and two scores; the doctor map proves the runnable-string part fits the budget when the data exists. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:541]

keyFindings.text: The cap does not bound the emitted brief: `capWithCompanion(head, …)` caps only the routing head, and `DIRECTIVES_LABEL + HYGIENE_DIRECTIVE` (13 + 205 = 218 characters ≈ 54 tokens) is appended after the cap [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:569]. Worst case the brief reaches 80 + 54 ≈ 134 tokens, and in the ambiguous branch 120 + 54 ≈ 174 tokens — above both the stated 80 and the maximum 120.

Measured composition: a typical normal brief is 268 characters ≈ 67 tokens, of which the routing head is 50 characters ≈ 13 tokens. So the routing payload — everything the model is supposed to act on — is about a fifth of the brief, and the directive block dominates it. There is room to add roughly one command line without raising the cap [INFERENCE: from the 50-character observed head and the 320-character head cap in render.ts:99].

The budget is not the blocker: the measured ambiguous head is about 86 characters, the full directive block about 205 characters, and a generic `Also: /speckit:plan <feature>` line is under 40 characters, all inside the 480-character ambiguous budget. The missing piece is structured command data, not space. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:185]

keyFindings.text: The no-match fallback carries no command either: `Advisor: no skill matched.` plus, only for setup-shaped prompts, `For setup or health checks, run /doctor:setup.` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:589]. So the one place a command *is* named on a miss is hardcoded to a single doctor command.

Consumer side: the repository tells the model to emit `SKILL ROUTING: [result]` from whatever the brief said [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:69]. With a brief that can only say "use {label}", the model's only faithful output is a skill name — the contract itself forbids the model from reporting a command it was never told.

Frontmatter tool grants cannot discriminate risk: all 45 commands declare `Bash`, 33 also declare `Write`/`Edit`, and the 12 that declare neither still mutate through shell calls (`/doctor:install`, `/doctor:update`, `/doctor:symlink`, `/doctor:git`, `/doctor:overlay` …) [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/install.md:1]. A risk classifier built on `allowed-tools` would call every command mutating and learn nothing.

Gate 2 says confidence at or above 0.8 requires skill invocation, but command workflows define their own execution modes. SpecKit planning asks for a mode when none is supplied; its mode table distinguishes :auto, :confirm and :autopilot. Confidence should select the workflow candidate, not silently choose the execution mode. The high-confidence invocation rule supports loading the command workflow; the required startup mode contradicts automatic execution without command inputs. [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:63-70] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/plan.md:29-35] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/plan.md:65-69]

The doctor route manifest is the only command set with an explicit mutation class. Its routes split into 16 `read-only`, 3 `add-only` and 22 `mutates` entries, and each carries a `gate3_location` naming what it writes. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:69] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:110]

25 of the 45 commands already accept an execution-mode suffix in their own `argument-hint` — `[:auto|:confirm]` — and the 20 that do not are exactly the 17 `/doctor:*` commands plus `/speckit:handoff`, `/speckit:save`, `/speckit:search` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/plan.md:1]. So the run-or-ask vocabulary already exists per command, as free text, and the two families that lack it lack it for opposite reasons: doctor has a machine-readable manifest instead, and the three speckit commands have no mode at all.

Startup defaults differ by command: create-agent binds an omitted mode to its confirm workflow, while SpecKit plan asks for a mode. Its :auto path runs autonomously and :confirm preserves checkpoint prompts. A registry needs command-specific defaultMode and askConditions; one global auto/confirm flag would misstate shipped workflows. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/agent.md:35-49] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/agent.md:65-70] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/plan.md:29-35]

The 19 command-metadata entries carry no mutation or safety field. Their schema is command, ownerMode, description, argumentHint, userIntent, choreography and discriminator, so a model cannot tell from the metadata whether `/create:skill` writes a new package or `/deep:review` only writes a review packet. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/command-metadata.json:3]

Every create command already ships a mode switch with the right semantics: `:auto` runs with no approval prompts and `:confirm` pauses at each step. Deep-research follows the same split (`approvals: none` in auto, `approvals: multi_gate` in confirm), and speckit-plan has both an interactive `step_by_step` branch and an autonomous `approvals: none` branch. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/README.txt:28] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-auto.yaml:26] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-confirm.yaml:11] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-plan.yaml:27]

`_routes.yaml` is the only machine-readable risk declaration in the tree: 33 route blocks plus 2 `mcp_subroutes` carry `mutating: read-only | add-only | mutates`, and most also carry `gate3_location`, a string naming the concrete file or database the route writes [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:41]. Tally across all 35 doctor bridges: 15 `read-only`, 2 `add-only`, 18 `mutates`.

The doctor git router blocks until a target is bound, does not infer a target from conversation history or workspace state, and shows a startup menu then waits when the target is missing. A strong route match can safely load the router, but cannot invent a positional target. The route's explicit argument forms are evidence against a blanket “ask before every command” rule: when the user supplied the target, this specific gate is satisfied. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/git.md:12-20]

The 15 `read-only` routes are the same 15 entries that carry `readOnly: true` in the TS projection, so the deriver's mapping `mutating === 'read-only' → readOnly: true` is verified end to end [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:305]. The risk signal already reaches the scorer; it stops before the JSON inventory and before the output contract.

The framework already has an ask-before-write rule: Gate 3 fires when a turn will create, edit, delete, move or generate a file, and explicitly does not fire for read-only review, audit, inspect, explain or analysis. It is a backstop after the model has chosen a workflow, not a signal at recommendation time. [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:72]

The reversibility ladder allows trivially reversible tracked-file edits and new files to proceed, but tier-3 sends, publishing, destructive migrations and external side effects require a written rollback and an explicit yes; approval does not transfer to later actions. This supports asking at the effect boundary, not before selecting every command. It contradicts both “always auto-run a high score” and “ask for every local write.” [SOURCE: .skilled/repo-rules/blast-radius.md:59-100]

Gate 3 asks a spec-folder question for writing routes, lets read-only routes proceed without a folder, and keeps the selected answer for the session. The ask should be attached to the chosen command's workflow and only when that workflow needs the missing choice. This supports route-specific questions; interactive Gate 3 is evidence against skipping all asks after a high-confidence match. [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:72-84]

No non-doctor source declares risk at all: `mutating` appears in none of the three `command-metadata.json` files, and `allow-list.json` carries only a free-text `reason` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/command-metadata.json:1]. The deriver's `readOnly` path is therefore starved for the other 28 commands because the data was never authored, not because the mechanism is missing.

The advisor's only safety mechanism is `readOnlyRouteAllowed`, which consults `skill.readOnly`. A mutating command that passes on a write-intent prompt is recommended with no ask marker, and the brief has no field to carry one. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/fusion.ts:686]

Name-based risk judgement fails in both directions: `/doctor:install`'s only route is `guide:read-only` (it prints an install guide, it does not install), while `/doctor:env`'s only route is `mutates` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:707]. "Install sounds dangerous" and "env sounds harmless" are both wrong, which is the argument for a declared field over a heuristic.

Recommended policy: carry a three-class safety map in the command inventory (`read-only`, `add-only`, `mutating`) plus the write root named by `gate3_location`; the model may start read-only commands immediately, may start add-only commands when the target path is explicit and bounded, and must ask before mutating commands or when the target is unclear. Put the authoritative class in each command's metadata and keep Gate 3 as the backstop. [INFERENCE: based on the doctor manifest's three classes and the missing field in command-metadata.json]

A three-tier reversibility ladder already governs this repository: trivially reversible (working-tree edit, new untracked file, local commit) proceeds, reversible-with-effort states the undo cost, and irreversible (sent/published/deleted-remote/force-push/non-allowlisted push) needs a written rollback plus an explicit yes; an install still waits for a yes [SOURCE: .skilled/repo-rules/blast-radius.md:47]. That is the vocabulary a command policy should reuse instead of inventing `safe`/`unsafe`.

Evidence against always asking for mutating commands: `:auto` is a shipped, first-class mode that intentionally runs without approval, and the create README documents it as a supported mode.
